summaries.demographer: Maria Buendia is a 34-year-old Mexican-born, U.S.-naturalized Latina woman living in Lilburn, GA (30047) with her husband Hector and their two children Lupita (14) and Mateo (11) (Q01, Q05, Q86-Q88). She completed tenth grade with no high school diploma and is currently enrolled in self-paced GED prep (Q01, Q90-Q92). Formally classified 'no occupation' but in practice a contract community liaison and freelance event planner earning ~$1,200/month against a household total of ~$5,000/month (Q65, Q72, Q74). The household owns their townhome in a multiethnic Lilburn subdivision (purchased 2017, FHA), participates in the ACA bronze market, and uses Peach Care for the children — a classic working-class immigrant-origin homeowner profile stretched across the Medicaid gap (Q36, Q40, Q58). Kin-dense network: parents and three siblings within the metro, Mother-in-law in Monterrey, grandmother in Guanajuato (Q05, Q06).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Maria exhibits strong pro-social, long-horizon orientation tempered by tight liquidity constraints. She uses a spreadsheet and envelope budgeting, participates in a $700-per-turn rotating tanda, and maintains a ~$2,400 emergency fund against ~$4,500 monthly spend (Q57, Q59, Q61, Q83). She is loss-averse around credit card debt (carrying ~$2,800 at 24% on a snowball plan) but willing to take strategic 0% APR on appliances (Q60, Q63). She turned down a fully funded Gwinnett Tech pastry scholarship at 26 after explicit napkin-math on family-hour losses — a vivid revealed-preference datum of family-over-individual utility (Q02, Q03). Strong peer-referral and word-of-mouth sensitivity — actively moderates information flow in her 800-member Facebook group and researched-and-banned a supplement scam, indicating above-average skepticism (Q17, Q42). Time preference skews patient (2-3 year GED/certification plan, 2027 Mexico trip savings, Lupita's quinceañera 18 months out) (Q62, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Maria is a highly engaged, reliably voting moderate Democrat (7/10 strength) with a self-described center-left, culturally Catholic political identity (Q23, Q24, Q95). She has voted in every general and midterm since her 2016 naturalization, organized two parish voter-registration drives that registered 140 voters in 2024, attended one BLM march (2020), and donated to The Bail Project (Q23, Q25, Q26, Q29). Her views are nuanced and cross-pressured: progressive on economic policy, immigration reform, Medicaid expansion, police reform, and a living wage; conservative-leaning on her personal abortion ethic while supporting legal access; pragmatic-skeptical about 'open borders' framing; open to local Republican candidates (Q24, Q95). She distrusts monolithic pan-Latino political framing and has had direct family-network political disagreements after 2024 (Q25). Institutional trust is mixed: trusts Dr. Chen, CDC, NPR, the Church, and her county commissioner Marlene Fosque; distrusts 287(g)-era law enforcement, WhatsApp forwards, and party-line oversimplifications (Q20, Q24, Q42).
summaries.psychologist: Maria presents as a conscientious, agreeable, moderately neurotic high-openness personality with strong collectivist-prosocial motivational architecture. Her self-concept is deeply identity-integrated around three pillars she names explicitly — family, faith, and service — and her narrative identity foregrounds sacrificial-caregiver arcs (leaving school, declining the scholarship) without expressed resentment, consistent with high agreeableness and religiously mediated meaning-making (Q01, Q02, Q109). She reports self-identified generalized anxiety and suspected untreated postpartum depression, managed through a coherent toolkit of yoga, prayer, journaling, social support (Cristina, Father Miguel, book club), and behavioral boundary-setting (news app deletion) — signaling good emotional granularity and adaptive coping, constrained by stigma and cost from accessing formal mental-health care (Q43-Q45, Q50). Cognitive style is methodical and planful (spreadsheets, envelope budgeting, GED structured prep) with a creative-synthesizing bent (fusion cooking, event choreography) (Q59, Q65). Relational style is warm, boundaried, and bridge-building across ethnic and political lines, with clear differentiation between intimate confidants (Cristina, mother) and community-role relationships (Q05, Q07, Q30).
